claim.summary: Over a field, on the cube {0,1}^n with C_D the degree-D part of the Boolean ideal, for a hypergraph H of nonempty blocks B with families (x_i)_{i in B}, approximators P_B in F[x_B] of degree <=a and K+a+1<=D: if each P_B is nonzero at some nonzero pattern of B, every common multiplier f (f P_B x_i in C_D) nonzero on the cube has degree >= tau(H), the transversal number; over F_p Pang's factors on a chain, prod_j(1-(x_{b_j}-x_{b_{j+1}})^(p-1)), nonzero exactly at 0 and 1_B, attain it with prod_{i in T}(1-x_i), T a least transversal, when tau(H)+a+1<=D. Over F_2 every product of s<=|B|-1 of Pang's factors meets the hypothesis, and s>=|B| factors allow f=1. Over F_2 on all (t+1)-subsets with t factors the least degree is n-t (attained when D>=n+1), the baseline prod(1+x_i) of degree n survives every choice, and for pairs (n>=4) a cyclic choice forces degree n; Pang's criterion S(1-eta)^t<1 with these t factors fails as an inequality at every 1<=K<=n when C(n,t+1)>=2^t, in particular for n>=2t+1.
claim.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with a follow-up (review record in research/results/common_multiplier_block_families_20261016); part (e) is the reviewer's construction, checked; the cube domain model only.

claim.summary: Over any field, on a finite product domain X = prod_j A_j (nonempty factors) with base states and one-hot variables x_(j,a) for non-base a (degree = least polynomial degree in them), a nonzero function vanishing on a union of cylinders (partial assignments) has degree at least the transversal number of their coordinate sets; if every coordinate of a least transversal T has a state no cylinder assigns there, the product of those state indicators (each of degree <=1) attains it. On the hole-respecting assignments of the product pigeonhole system, with base state empty, the least degree of a nonzero function vanishing on the supports of monomial errors on distinct holes is the transversal number of their hole sets, which is the least degree of a surviving common killer of 1 when tau<=K and K+e is inert, or D=n with K+e<=n and K<=n-1; for tau>K there is none of degree <=K.

claim.summary: Over any field, on the Boolean cube {0,1}^N, let U be an up-set with minimal sets M. The functions given by polynomials of degree <=d vanishing on U have the basis prod_{v in T}(1-x_v) over the transversals T of M (sets meeting every member) with |T|<=d; so their dimension is the number of such transversals and the least degree of a nonzero one is the transversal number tau(M). For a function p, the least degree of such an f with fp nonzero is the least size of a transversal avoiding some point of supp p (infinite if supp p lies in U). Hence for monomial errors c_j x_(A_j), among killers f with deg f+max|A_j|<=D, a common killer modulo the cube's degree-D vanishing ideal that keeps 1 alive exists exactly when tau({A_j})+max|A_j|<=D, of least degree tau({A_j}) (none for a constant error); for Pang's t=1 families over F2 with inputs exactly x_a, x_b and q=x_a+x_b it is the vertex-cover number of the input graph.
claim.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer in a staged goal review; the degree window, the Gallai conditions and the relation to the greedy certificate are its corrections.

claim.summary: Over F_p, for a degree-D pseudoideal containing the Boolean axioms, families (g_mu,i) of degree<=d with approximators P_mu of degree<=a, kernels Z_mu(k), joint kernel Z(k), joint rank phi(k), W_nu(k) the joint kernel of the other families and marginal m_nu(k)=dim W_nu(k)-dim Z(k), with K>=d and a+K+pd<=D: phi(k)/N_n(k) is nonincreasing (Pang's Lemma 4.1 for intersections); some q in family nu's span makes P_nu(1-q^(p-1)) enlarge the joint kernel by at least (1-1/p)m_nu(K-d) (Pang's Lemma 4.2 on the subspace W_nu(K-d)), and every refinement of family nu alone by at most m_nu(K). All marginals can vanish with full joint rank (F_2, the degree-3 vanishing ideal of {0,1}^2, K=d=1, families {1+y},{x+y},{y}, phi=3), so refining one family at a time has no per-step contraction of the joint rank. One simultaneous round can gain nothing too: F_2, the degree-4 vanishing ideal of {0,1}^4, K=d=1, P=1, the six pair families {x_i,x_j}: every choice of q_ij leaves the joint kernel 0 (Sauer-Shelah), with phi(1)=5 and phi(0)=1.

claim.summary: Under Pang v1 Theorem4.3's Boolean F_p setup, proper C_D, S fixed degree<=d families, 1<=d<=K<=n,t>=1, Delta=(p-1)dt and Delta+K+d<=D, choose approximators with error ranks <=H(1-eta)^t, eta=(1-1/p)N_n(K-d)/N_n(K), H=dim V_K/(C_D intersect V_K). After adaptive choices, an auxiliary base-field bilinear form and a p-linear observation realization have radical exactly the stacked error kernel on that quotient. S(1-eta)^t<1 gives the original surviving multilinear multiplier. The original simulation separately pays K+max(2Delta+2d,Delta+w)<=D. The established binary leveled choice order and constructive error-correcting-pair observable kernel are preserved. The preceding full-space native moment theorem uses the sufficient reserve Delta+d+pK<=D, not implied by the original selection cutoff. No contraction rate, decoder or source lower bound is improved.
claim.assessment: Working matched representation calibration passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer and correction check; primary recurrence and constructive coding estimates retained as dependencies. Nonvacuity is selection-only, and the native reserve is sufficient rather than necessary.
